domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on GitHub Advanced Security's code scanning, secret scanning, and AI-powered vulnerability remediation as a security platform. The content addresses security operations tooling built into a developer platform used by software builders. Security scanning and auto-fix occur during development in PRs, while alert monitoring and coverage views operate across production repositories. The talk assumes familiarity with software security concepts but remains accessible to a general AI engineering audience. Recorded conference presentation with live product demo at AI Engineer World's Fair. All evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript.

summary: Sarah Khalife, a Principal Solutions Engineer at GitHub for 4.5 years, presents on GitHub's AI-powered security platform at the AI Engineer World's Fair. She frames the talk around GitHub incorporating AI across the entire platform, not just Copilot, with a focus on the security pillar. GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) integrates application security into the developer platform with three main capabilities: code scanning using CodeQL (an open-source query language that analyzes data flow to find vulnerabilities, with community-backed queries from Microsoft, Google, Uber, and others), secret scanning (which detects API keys and custom secrets across repositories, Git history, and pull request comments, with push protection proactively blocking secrets before exposure), and supply chain security via Dependabot. Khalife highlights that secret scanning is the biggest win across her customers, with partner integrations reaching approximately 99.9% accuracy. The session then explores how AI benefits security through easier identification, faster remediation, and driving productivity. Three AI-powered features are detailed: code scanning auto fix, which provides AI-generated fix suggestions in pull requests powered by CodeQL data flow context, with customers reporting roughly 70% success and available in public beta; custom pattern generation, where AI helps generate regex patterns for secret scanning, simplifying a task customers previously did via ChatGPT or Google; and unstructured password detection, which uses AI analysis to identify true positive passwords exposed in Git history. A live demo follows, showing the GitHub organization security tab with 73,000 alerts in a demo repository, a coverage view revealing secret scanning at 99% but code scanning at only 57%, code scanning alerts with source-to-sink vulnerability paths, and auto-fix providing specific remediation suggestions for a cross-site scripting vulnerability in a pull request. The demo concludes with the AI suggesting installation of an escape HTML library to resolve the vulnerability, which the developer can review, commit, and trigger re-scans to verify remediation. Khalife closes by noting additional AI security examples—including AI-generated secret detection—are available at the Microsoft booth.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Platform Overview
sections.summary: Sarah Khalife introduces herself as a Principal Solutions Engineer at GitHub of 4.5 years, working primarily with financial services customers. She contextualizes the talk within the broader GitHub ecosystem, noting that while Copilot has been discussed extensively, GitHub is incorporating AI across the entire platform including collaboration, productivity, and security. She emphasizes improving AppSec with AI rather than just discussing security around AI.

sections.title: GitHub Scale and Community
sections.summary: Khalife shares GitHub's scale metrics: over 100 million developers, 4 million organizations, and 90% of Fortune 100 companies. She emphasizes that community feedback from customers, vendors, and partners drives feature development and platform improvement.

sections.title: GitHub Advanced Security Introduction
sections.summary: Introduces GHAS as integrating application security into the developer platform with a GitHub-native experience. Khalife previews the three main features to be covered: code scanning, secret scanning, and supply chain security, with AI enhancements.

sections.title: Code Scanning and CodeQL
sections.summary: Covers code scanning using CodeQL, an open-source query language that analyzes data flow to detect vulnerabilities. Emphasizes community-backed queries from Microsoft, Google, and Uber. Discusses third-party integrations via SARIF for capabilities like container scanning that CodeQL does not cover natively.

sections.title: Secret Scanning and Push Protection
sections.summary: Describes secret scanning as the biggest customer win, detecting API keys and custom secrets across repositories and Git history. Push protection proactively blocks secrets before they enter commit history. Partner-based detection reaches approximately 99.9% accuracy.

sections.title: Supply Chain Security and Shared Responsibility
sections.summary: Introduces Dependabot for detecting vulnerable dependencies, with AI components in early development. Closes by emphasizing security as a shared responsibility integrated into developers' day-to-day work, not solely an AppSec mandate.

sections.title: AI Benefits for Security and Code Scanning Auto Fix
sections.summary: Explains that AI benefits security through easier identification, faster remediation, and driving productivity. Introduces code scanning auto fix as the most exciting AI feature, providing AI-generated fix suggestions in pull requests powered by CodeQL data flow context. Customers report approximately 70% success rate. The feature is in public beta.

sections.title: Secret Scanning AI Improvements
sections.summary: Details two AI improvements for secret scanning: custom pattern generation, where AI suggests regex patterns based on sample inputs, simplifying a task customers previously did manually via ChatGPT or Google; and unstructured password detection, which uses AI analysis to identify true positive passwords exposed in Git history, initially labeled as 'other' due to expected false positives.

sections.title: Demo: Organization Security Overview and Coverage View
sections.summary: Begins live demo showing the GitHub organization security tab with 73,000 open alerts in a demo repository. Highlights the coverage view as her favorite, revealing that secret scanning covers 99% of repositories but code scanning only 57%, exposing gaps in protection especially for repositories not going through CI pipelines.

sections.title: Demo: Code Scanning Alerts and Auto Fix in Pull Requests
sections.summary: Shows code scanning alert details with source-to-sink vulnerability paths, where CodeQL identifies multiple paths to the same sink. Transitions to a pull request demo where a developer introduced a cross-site scripting vulnerability, and GitHub Advanced Security provides AI-powered auto-fix suggesting installation of the escape HTML library. Khalife emphasizes the developer still reviews the fix before committing, and committing triggers re-scans to verify remediation. She closes by noting additional AI secret detection examples are available at the Microsoft booth.
